model_notes.package: PyHierarchicalTsetlinMachineCUDA.tm.TsetlinMachine at upstream commit 5b4a223075c1e621577d508bc7c3c061230e29d5 installed from GitHub into .venv-htm (env/htm_install.sh, env/htm.lock; results/20260925T032750Z_htm_env_install), with its four switches as listed per model (binary_inference, constant_update_p, and_group_normalization, no_clipping), weighted_clauses False, grid (208,1,1), block (128,1,1), seed = world seed. hier: ((AND_GROUP, 2000), (OR_ALTERNATIVES, alternatives), (AND_ALTERNATIVES, n_concepts)), 'clauses' clauses; flat: ((AND_GROUP, 2000), (AND_GROUP, 1)), clauses x alternatives x n_concepts clauses.
model_notes.selection: a model with more than one grid point is selected on validation bags (val combinations carved from the training combinations, 20 percent) after fitting on bags of the other 80 percent, then refit on all training bags; ties to the first grid point. LR chooses C by 4-fold CV inside the training bags. The test bags are scored once per seed.

control.note: Granmo's examples/NoisyParityDemo.py and NoisyParityData.py of the package (200,000 examples each, noise on training labels only, the demo's argparse defaults: 32 clauses, T 250, s 25.0, 7 state bits, boost 0); pass = clean test accuracy >= 0.90 before 1,000 epochs or 7,200 s, whichever comes first (the package README shows 99.71 percent after 778 epochs); stops at the first evaluation that passes

verdict.rule: H17.5 (docs/13 A7): over seeds 1 to 5, the hierarchical package's mean held-out accuracy is at least 0.90 AND at least the flat package's mean plus 0.20; primary pair htm_hier_neg vs htm_flat_neg (append_negated=True, the package default), secondary pair htm_hier_pos vs htm_flat_pos (append_negated=False) reported next to it; paired per-seed differences with a Student-t interval and the one-sided Wilcoxon signed-rank p

checks.head_off_vs_c85: [measured] HEAD with the switches off reproduces c85ca4e7 h37 exactly at epochs 1 and 10 (e0; h25 again), then diverges (h25 differs from c85 h37 from epoch 20, f25 from c85 f37 from epoch 10, the noisy-parity control from epoch 1). [derived from the two kernels.py] c85ca4e7 compares curand_uniform with 1.0*|y - class_sum|/(2*THRESHOLD) in double precision, HEAD with fabsf(y - class_sum)/(2*THRESHOLD) in single precision, so a rare draw lands on different sides and the chaotic trajectory separates; the dynamics are the same in distribution (h25 val 0.750 vs c85 h37 0.708, f25 0.814 vs c85 f37 0.814 at their best epochs). docs/12 F26 (3) holds as 'same algorithm', not as 'bit-identical'.
